story_type: docking target arrives with its shroud stuck half open, Gemini 9, 1967 program film
hook: Their docking target showed up with its jaws hanging open.
narration: Their docking target showed up in orbit with its jaws hanging open.
On Gemini 9, an Atlas rocket failed to put the first target, an Agena, into orbit, so a substitute was launched.
A shroud protects the docking end during launch and should split away in orbit. This one failed to separate.
[short pause] The astronauts quickly named it the angry alligator. Docking had to be canceled.
outcome: The flight plan was revised on the spot, and the crew practiced rendezvous with the angry alligator two more times.
title: Docking target had its jaws open
description:
On Gemini 9, a substitute docking target reached orbit with its launch shroud stuck half open, and the astronauts named it the angry alligator. Docking was canceled and the crew practiced rendezvous with it two more times. From the 1967 NASA film The Legacy of Gemini.

facts.source_quote: On Gemini 9, when an Atlas rocket failed to place the Agena into orbit,
a substitute docking target was launched.
Trouble developed on the new target when its shroud failed to separate,
leaving what the astronauts quickly named the angry alligator.
Although the docking maneuver had to be canceled, the flight plan was revised,
so the astronauts could go on to practice rendezvous two more times,
